claims.text: QueuedOrder holds idempotencyKey, subject (the customer's sub, the access-token field identifying the signed-in user), description, items (OrderItemRequest with unitPriceVnd the customer saw) and status, which defaults to QueuedOrderStatus.waiting.

OrderQueue (a Riverpod Notifier) keeps orders oldest first under localStorage key 'donhang.order_queue'; build() reads it back; add/remove/mark* go through _save, which writes the JSON to the store and only then sets state.

Stage-3 ApiClient.createOrder sends the Idempotency-Key header; http.ClientException → ApiUnreachable; status 502, 503 or 504 → ApiUnreachable (checked before 201); any other non-201 → ApiProblem.fromResponse.

package:http reports a request that gets no response (connection refused, network error; on the web, a failed fetch) by throwing http.ClientException; the same type also covers other client-side failures, such as a closed client.
claims.source_hint: http 1.6.0 source: lib/src/exception.dart ClientException; io_client.dart (SocketException → ClientException); browser_client.dart (failed fetch rethrown as ClientException)

claims.text: DonHang.App calls the API through Caddy on :8080, which proxies /api/v1/* to DonHang.Api; the comment above createOrder (outside the excerpt) reads 502/503/504 as the proxy in front of the API saying it could not reach the API.

_submit calls newIdempotencyKey() once per press, before createOrder; on ApiUnreachable it calls _queue with that key; on ApiProblem it shows problem.detail; on any other Exception the orderFailed message. Flutter's State.mounted is false once the State has been removed from the tree (disposed).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.App/lib/screens/create_order_screen.dart:58-80; Flutter API docs: State.mounted

claims.text: `_queue`, below the excerpt, reads the signed-in customer's `sub` from the token, adds a `QueuedOrder` holding the same `idempotencyKey`, and goes to `/orders/queued`; with no `sub` it queues nothing and shows the general message.
A later send of a queued order passes the stored order.idempotencyKey to createOrder.
At stage-3, POST /api/v1/orders with an Idempotency-Key already used by that customer returns the earlier order and does not store another.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs:27-57 (PlaceOrderAsync returns created=false); DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs; backend.l2.idempotent-endpoints

claims.text: The `Waiting orders` screen (`lib/screens/queued_orders_screen.dart`) lists the signed-in customer's queued orders; a waiting one shows `Waiting to be sent:` followed by the quantity and product name, and no order number.
The order number is OrderResult.id from the API's 201 body; a QueuedOrder has no id of its own, only a result set after the API answered.

test/api_client_test.dart at stage-3 has 7 tests against a fake http.Client (201 with key, 502/503/504, no response, 400, 429); flutter test ends with 'All tests passed!'. With const [502, 504], 'a 503 from the proxy means no answer' fails and the other six pass.

claims.text: Queue only when the outcome is unknown (no answer). Any other status, a 500 included, is the API's answer and is shown in the form; a 400, for example, is a refusal of this exact order that the customer at the form can fix, and sent again unchanged it is refused again.
